summary: After one failed `make setup` (default python3 = 3.11), the documented interpreter override `make setup PYTHON=python3.12` fails with the identical error, because `$(PYTHON) -m venv .venv` does not recreate the existing venv; .venv/bin/python keeps pointing to 3.11 while pyvenv.cfg claims 3.12.3.
expected: README.md 'Commands' + setup paragraph: `make setup` is the once-per-clone setup and 'Build with a specific interpreter via `make setup PYTHON=python3.14`'; the tools 'fail fast with the setup command if a dependency is missing'. Expected the override to recover from the first failure.
actual: Attempt 1 `make setup` exit 2: pip 'ERROR: Package 'learningos-core' requires a different Python: 3.11.15 not in '>=3.12''. Attempt 2 `make setup PYTHON=python3.12` exit 2 with the same pip error ('Requirement already satisfied: pip in ./.venv/lib/python3.11/site-packages'). .venv/bin/python -> python3 -> /usr/local/bin/python3 (3.11.15); a python3.12 symlink was added beside it. No documentation mentions deleting or recreating .venv. Recovered only with `rm -rf .venv && make setup PYTHON=python3.12` (exit 0).
reproduction: On a host whose `python3` is 3.11 and where python3.12 is installed, in a fresh world: make setup   # exit 2
make setup PYTHON=python3.12   # exit 2, same error
own_error_possible: README does state 'Python 3.12+ is required', and S00 had already shown that the default interpreter is 3.11, so running `make setup PYTHON=python3.12` first would have avoided the failure. The defect is only that the failed state cannot be recovered with the documented override.

summary: Running the documented `make test-fast` inside the learner's installation wrote 135 trace spans to the learner's own operations/diagnostics/traces.jsonl. `los operations` now reports a request the learner never made: `req-bad-payload` (capability `unknown.write`, canonical_outcome AMBIGUOUS, recovery_requirement reconcile-exact-request, needs_attention true).
expected: README 'Commands': 'make test-fast  # quick feedback: synthetic fixtures, no checked-in repository load'. Expected tests to leave the repository's operational state untouched.
actual: Before (observer S01-before): operations/diagnostics held only .gitkeep and `los operations` was empty. After: traces.jsonl, 54,128 bytes, one trace_id b3374ba2d506605f0e90a7e68fc300f5, spans timestamped 2026-09-24T23:34:47–23:35:03Z. That window falls inside the test-fast run: views finished 23:33:52, pytest cache written 23:45:52, and no other command ran in it. The file is gitignored, so git status stays clean, but the product's own operations view shows it as needing attention.
reproduction: fresh world, after a working .venv: .venv/bin/python tools/los.py operations   # {"operations": []}
tools/los.py operations   # req-bad-payload, AMBIGUOUS, needs_attention true
own_error_possible: The test suite is developer tooling, and a learner might not be expected to run it inside their own repository. But README lists make test-fast among the ordinary commands without warning that it touches repository state. I did not bisect which test wrote the trace (that would require reading tests/**). The container runs as uid 0, which might change which tests reach the real repository path. Also, this agent session's environment sets TRACEPARENT=00-b3374ba2d506605f0e90a7e68fc300f5-…, and LearningOS adopts it as the trace/operation id (seen again in S26). The 45 'attempts' under one request id may therefore be several distinct test requests collapsed into one operation by the shared ambient trace id, rather than one request retried 45 times.

summary: `make test-fast`, documented as 'synthetic fixtures, no checked-in repository load', fails 34 of 2,278 tests in a learner installation (11 min 54 s). At least 17 of the failures raise FileNotFoundError for files that exist only in the product author's repository (work/active/workspace-m2-exam-prep/outputs/sad-l06-chapter-summaries/*.md, operations/transactions/transaction-20260920-*.yaml) or KeyError on scenario ids S9/S10/S11.
expected: README 'Commands': make test-fast = 'quick feedback: synthetic fixtures, no checked-in repository load'; `make` help: 'run tests that do not load the checked-in repository state'.
actual: 34 failed, 2214 passed, 30 skipped, 83 deselected in 713.67s. Failing groups: test_pilot_replay (17, missing author workspace files and transaction receipts); test_operations (4, newest-first ordering and COMMITTED vs NOT_COMMITTED); test_causal_resolver (5); test_diagnostic_store (2); test_recovery_conflicts (3) and test_diagnostic_store::test_no_exception_body_reaches_the_store (these inject faults with chmod 0o555, which does not stop uid 0, so body['error'] is None); test_gateway_v2 (1); test_format_fixtures (1, KeyError 'title'); test_abilities (1, StopIteration). A single re-run of test_pilot_replay.py + test_operations.py reproduced deterministically: 21 failed, 12 passed in 12.3 s.
reproduction: fresh world with working .venv (as uid 0): make test-fast   # exit 2, 34 failed
minimized: .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/test_pilot_replay.py tests/test_operations.py -q -p no:cacheprovider   # 21 failed, 12 passed
own_error_possible: About 6 failures are probably environmental: the container runs as root, so chmod-based fault injection cannot work. The world is a synthetic installation rather than the author's clone, but that is exactly a learner's situation. I did not run the suite on the product repository to compare, so some failures may also occur there.

summary: The README's inbox capture command (`python tools/los.py capture --text "…"`) is refused. The only working path is a hand-built GatewayEnvelopeV2. Building one needs two things no document gives: how `intent_sha256` is computed, and the fact that capture.create must guard a synthetic artifact `capture-request:<idempotency_key>` in expected_revisions. Both were found only by reading tools/learning_os/contracts/gateway.py.
expected: README.md 'Start here' item 2: 'capture anything into work/inbox/ (or `python tools/los.py capture --text "…"`)'. CLAUDE.md §3 / §14 treat inbox capture as an automatic permission. OPERATOR.md: 'Read the payload schema, then submit one envelope (fields and intent hash: WORKFLOWS §25a, step 4)'.
actual: `los.py capture --text "ask tutor about lasso subgradients"` exits 2 with 'canonical writes must use GatewayEnvelopeV2; direct CLI application is disabled — apply it with `los capability capture.create --payload-file ENVELOPE.json`'. WORKFLOWS §25a step 4 says only that approval.subject_sha256 is `intent_sha256(envelope)`, and AI-ACTIONS.md calls it 'the standard Gateway V2 hash over that whole intent'; neither gives the algorithm. `capabilities capture.create --json` lists writes ['work/inbox/**'] and payload fields but no expected_revisions key. CLI help has no envelope-preparing command, and `capture` has no --check. After reading gateway.py (intent_subject/intent_sha256, REQUEST_SCOPED_ARTIFACT_PREFIXES), an envelope with expected_revisions {capture-request:<key>: 0}, built with the product's own functions, committed on the first attempt.
reproduction: fresh world, working interpreter: python tools/los.py capture --text "ask tutor about lasso subgradients"   # exit 2, refusal
python tools/los.py capabilities capture.create --json   # no mention of the capture-request:<key> revision guard
grep -rn intent_sha256 system/ README.md   # the name is used, never defined
successful workaround needs: from learning_os.contracts.gateway import intent_sha256, request_artifact_id
own_error_possible: An interface (the Obsidian UI) may build this envelope for a human learner, and the product may expect agents to reuse its gateway helpers. But OPERATOR.md, the entry point for agents, names no helper, and the README one-liner is presented as a human fallback that works without the UI. I guessed revision 0 for the new request artifact, and it was accepted.
